title: Canonical Signal Record
description: Schema for a canonical signal file in .moeb/signals/catalogue/.

signal_id.description: Canonical UUID v4 identifier. Stable across all occurrences and status transitions. Never reused or reassigned. Also the filename stem: <signal_id>.signal.json.

category.description: Classifies the signal by the kind of improvement it represents. Error: a recoverable failure that degraded run quality or caused a rubric violation. NewCapability: a missing moeb tool or feature that forced an external or unsupported workaround. SkillImprovement: a skill file instruction that produced suboptimal or incorrect agent behaviour. ToolImprovement: a moeb tool implementation defect that did not cause complete failure but increased cost or produced incorrect output. ProcessImprovement: a gap in the run, spec, or fix_signal workflow lifecycle that caused unnecessary manual intervention. ReasoningImprovement: a systematic reasoning or judgement gap that led to suboptimal decisions.

signal_source.description: Origin of the signal. 'moeb': relates to the moeb harness itself (baseline rubric criteria, skill execution quality, tool capability gaps, kernel behaviour). 'project': relates to the project under development with moeb (project-specific rubric criteria, layers 3-4). Default when indeterminate: 'moeb'.

severity.description: Impact on run quality. Critical: caused a rubric failure, data corruption, or required significant recovery work (e.g. full file rewrite). Major: caused measurable degradation — extra tool calls, partial output loss, or repeated retries — without complete failure. Minor: a process or guidance gap with low immediate impact but recurring cost if unaddressed. Info: an observation worth tracking with no immediate quality impact.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary used as the index label and fix_signal selection display. Should be unique across the catalogue and unambiguous without context.

description.description: Full narrative of what happened: observed symptoms, recovery path taken, relevant file paths or tool names, and why the issue recurs. Must be sufficient for a spec author to understand root cause without reading the run trace.

proposed_resolution.description: Actionable description of what a fixing specification should accomplish. Used verbatim as the requirement passed to start_spec by fix_signal. Null only when no resolution is known at signal creation time.

gating_condition.description: Array of signal_id UUIDs that must each have status: resolved before fix_signal may pick up this signal. null or empty array means no gate. Example: ["a1000040-0601-4000-8000-000000000040"]

status.description: Lifecycle state of the signal. open: the issue persists and no fix has been applied; eligible for fix_signal selection. in_progress: fix_signal has selected and marked this signal with picked_up_at; spec authoring is in progress. spec_written: a specification has been authored and registered in the harness README. candidate: the run implementing the specification passed QA review and a candidate tag was created. resolved: the issue was accepted via accept_candidate and a resolved event was emitted. superseded: a different design decision made the proposed_resolution unnecessary (see links). reopened: a previously resolved signal has recurred and is eligible for re-selection by fix_signal. rejected: intentionally not going to be addressed. archived: closed and moved to archive/catalogue/ via archive_signal.

links.description: References to artifacts that explain the signal's lifecycle transitions. Expected when status is resolved, superseded, or archived; may be omitted when open. Each entry names an artifact type, its identifier, and the relationship type.

artifactType.description: The kind of artifact being referenced. spec: a moeb specification file, identified by domain.slug. signal: another signal in the catalogue, identified by its UUID signal_id. run: a moeb run artifact, identified by its UUID run_id. branch: a git branch, identified by its branch name.

id.description: Identifier of the referenced artifact. Format varies by artifactType — spec: '<domain>.<slug>' (e.g. 'moeb.deprecate-patch-file-as-default-write-path'); signal: UUID v4 signal_id; run: UUID v4 run_id; branch: git branch name (e.g. 'feat/fix-<slug>').

type.description: Nature of the relationship. superseded_by: the referenced artifact adopted a different approach that made this signal's proposed_resolution unnecessary. resolved_by: the referenced artifact directly implemented the fix described in proposed_resolution. related_to: informational cross-reference with no lifecycle dependency. caused_by: the referenced artifact introduced the condition or regression that triggered this signal. fix: the referenced branch was created by fix_signal to autonomously resolve this signal.

occurrence_count.description: Total number of times this signal condition has been observed across all runs. Must equal the length of the occurrences array.

first_seen.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the first recorded occurrence. Equals occurrences[0].timestamp.

last_seen.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent occurrence. Equals first_seen when occurrence_count is 1.

occurrences.description: Ordered list of individual occurrences, oldest first. Each entry records when the signal condition was observed and in which run.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of this individual occurrence.

run_id.description: UUID of the moeb run in which this occurrence was observed.

picked_up_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp set by fix_signal when this signal is selected for autonomous resolution. Absence means the signal has not been picked up. Presence prevents re-selection by subsequent fix_signal invocations.

resolved_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp set by accept_candidate when the signal is marked resolved. Absent on all other status values.

resolution_summary.description: Human-readable explanation of how the signal was resolved. Set by accept_candidate or archive_signal. Null until resolved.

archived_on.description: ISO 8601 timestamp set by archive_signal when the file is moved to archive/catalogue/. Null until archived.
